stories.title: Man United earn 4-4 draw against Aston Villa but remain in relegation zone
stories.description: Michael Carrick's team continue forgettable season with last-gasp draw at Old Trafford in front of angry home fans.
stories.excerpt: Michael Carrick’s team continues its forgettable season with a 4-4 defeat at Old Trafford in front of angry home fans. Manchester United pulled off a dramatic late comeback to earn a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in front of their angry home fans amid a torrid time at the Premier League club. United conceded two goals within the first four minutes of the high-stakes fixture at Old Trafford in Manchester on Sunday, but fought back with two stoppage-time goals and shared the spoils. The 13-time Premier League champions remain in the relegation zone in the Premier League table, sitting in 18th place with eight points from 10 games. But their manager Michael Carrick will breathe a sigh of relief after avoiding a fifth loss and will again hope to avoid getting sacked. Carrick was seconds away from heading into the international break on the back of another devastating defeat that would surely have led to his dismissal. stories.title: Leeds condemn racist abuse of Bogle after Tel incident
stories.description: Leeds United condemn the "disgusting" online racist abuse directed towards defender Jayden Bogle following Saturday's 1-0 win against Tottenham.
stories.excerpt: Leeds United have condemned the "disgusting" online racist abuse directed towards defender Jayden Bogle following Saturday's 1-0 win against Tottenham. The 26-year-old Leeds defender was targeted after he escaped punishment for a first-half tackle on Mathys Tel that led to the Spurs forward hobbling off. The full-back caught the back of Tel's ankle with his studs but referee John Brooks decided not to punish him following a lengthy video assistant referee review. Tottenham are set to submit a formal complaint about the decision to not send Bogle off and will write to refereeing body Pro Ref to seek an explanation. Leeds said they had been "appalled" by the racist abuse posted on social media about Bogle, adding it condemned the behaviour "in the strongest possible terms". "There is no place for racism in football or society," a club statement read. stories.title: After the midterms, where does the Republican Party stand?
stories.description: GOP suffered a loss, but it is hardly a historic one. A party in power has always been held to account in the midterms.
stories.excerpt: The GOP suffered a loss, but it is hardly a historic one. A party in power has always been held to account in the midterms. On Tuesday, the United States held midterm elections. Every one of the 435 seats in the US House of Representatives was up for election and 35 of the 100 US Senate seats were on the ballot. The result of the elections was overwhelmingly in favour of the Democratic Party, or the blue team, as the US media has taken to referring to them. It was a blue wave. A blue tsunami. Democrats flipped at least 40 House seats and seven Senate seats. It was a clear message to Washington that much of the US is unhappy with the direction the country is headed. Texas had not elected a Democrat in a statewide race for more than 30 years. Democrats dominated in Texas. Kansas hadn’t sent a Democrat to the Senate since 1932. stories.description: Xabi Alonso's frustration is evident as Chelsea's struggles for an identity continue with the disappointing 1-0 defeat by Sunderland.
stories.excerpt: Constant changes in formation and personnel - and another disappointing defeat. Xabi Alonso's frustration was obvious as Chelsea's struggles for identity continued in the 1-0 defeat by Sunderland. It is starting to feel as though the Spaniard is the latest "Tinkerman" at Stamford Bridge, a moniker first associated with Blues boss Claudio Ranieri back in 2002-03. For the first time this season, Chelsea lined up with a three-man midfield - but they were also without a recognised striker for the second match in a row, with Pedro Neto again struggling to lead the line in their loss at the Stadium of Light. By contrast, struggling Sunderland were led by target man Brian Brobbey, who won a 36th-minute penalty after being brought down by Levi Colwill. Enzo le Fee converted the game's only goal from the spot. stories.title: First Derry goal worth the wait for final hero Burns
stories.description: Derry City's FAI Cup final hero Darragh Burns says there is "nowhere better" to get his first goal for the club than scoring the winner at the Aviva Stadium in the decider.
stories.excerpt: Derry City's FAI Cup hero Darragh Burns said there is "nowhere better" to get his first goal for the club than at the Aviva Stadium in a final. Burns' low drive on 69 minutes broke the deadlock for the Candystripes against a spirited Waterford and was enough to secure the club's seventh FAI Cup victory. The 24-year-old was set to be substituted before he fired home and was relieved to contribute with his first goal since arriving at the club in July. "I saw the substitutions getting going and I said to myself 'please just produce something' and it went in the back of the net so I'm over the moon," he told BBC Sport NI's Odhran Crumley. "It took me longer than I expected to score my first goal, but nowhere better to get it than at the Aviva in the cup final. I dreamt of it last night and it's come true today. stories.description: Kozo Tashima believes he has a '20 to 30 percent' chance of winning the FIFA presidency election against Infantino.
stories.excerpt: Kozo Tashima believes he has a ’20 to 30 percent’ chance of winning the FIFA presidency election against Infantino. The latest challenger to FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s re-election bid, Kozo Tashima, believes he has a 20 to 30 percent chance of winning the coveted seat in global football. Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA), said governance is FIFA’s biggest problem as he outlined his platform for next year’s presidential election on Sunday. “I’ve received many messages saying, ‘Thank you for speaking out’…,” Tashima told Japanese daily Sports Nippon. Tashima announced on Thursday that he intended to run in the March election, becoming the first Japanese candidate to seek world football’s top job. stories.title: Qatar runner-up Marquez must wait for eighth title
stories.description: Spaniard Marc Marquez misses the chance to clinch a record-equalling eighth MotoGP title after finishing second in Sunday's Qatar Grand Prix.
stories.excerpt: Marc Marquez will have to wait to seal a record-equalling eighth MotoGP title after finishing second behind Marco Bezzecchi in the Qatar Grand Prix. The 33-year-old Spaniard won Saturday's sprint race and would have clinched a second successive title, drawing level with Valentino Rossi's record tally, had main rival Jorge Martin finished outside the points in Sunday's grand prix. However, Martin - the 2024 champion - returned from injury after withdrawing from the previous race with a fractured wrist to finish seventh. Ducatti rider Marquez has a 60-point lead over Aprilia's Martin and will have another chance to clinch the title in the season's penultimate race weekend in Portimao, Portugal, in two weeks' time. Pole-sitter Bezzecchi, Martin's Aprilia team-mate, claimed his sixth grand prix win of the season, while Spain's Trackhouse Aprilia rider Raul Fernandez was third. stories.title: Bicycle ‘boycott ride’ targeting Jewish-owned businesses in Philadelphia draws hundreds of counterprotesters
stories.description: A bicycle “boycott ride” targeting several Jewish-owned businesses in Philadelphia took place Sunday amid a large police presence and crowds of counterprotesters lining both sides of the street for blocks.
stories.excerpt: A bicycle “boycott ride” targeting several Jewish-owned businesses in Philadelphia took place Sunday amid a large police presence and crowds of counterprotesters lining both sides of the street for blocks. The demonstration, widely condemned by state and local leaders, drew what appeared to be hundreds of counterprotesters and sparked some verbal confrontations. The protest fell the day before the 88th anniversary of Kristallnacht and was organized by Philly Bike On Your Left, a group that describes itself as “anti-Zionist” and says it targeted the businesses because of their owners’ support for Israel. “Ride around Rittenhouse with us as we show these zionist business owners that we see them for the disgusting humans they are,” the group said in its original October 30 Instagram post announcing the ride. As the cyclists began their ride Sunday, counterprotesters waved Israeli flags and held signs condemning antisemitism. CNN witnessed police leading some protesters away from the crowd

stories.title: It's not 'colonialism', it's 'invasion': Burkina Faso corrects Africa's history
stories.description: The government subsequently distributed a 190-page guide to teachers to support implementation, pending the production of revised textbooks.
stories.excerpt: Burkina Faso has introduced sweeping changes to its school curriculum under President Ibrahim Traoré, replacing colonial-era terminology and adding lessons intended to strengthen African identity, patriotism and national pride. The reforms, which took effect at the start of the 2026–27 academic year on October 1, cover history, geography and civic education. Under the new guidelines, ‘colonisation’ is described as ‘imperialist invasion’, while ‘colonisers’ become ‘invaders’ and European explorers are referred to as ‘spies’. The term ‘ethnic groups’ is also replaced with ‘socio-cultural groups’. The changes go beyond terminology. New history lessons examine African resistance, indigenous knowledge, Burkina Faso’s revolutionary history and the 1791–1804 Haitian Revolution. The curriculum also introduces the history of the Alliance of Sahel States, formed by Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger. Geography lessons are being revised to remove descriptions such as ‘poor country’, ‘indebted country’

rejected.excerpt: Alcaraz bagged a 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 straight sets for an elusive Paris crown before the year-end ATP Finals. Carlos Alcaraz has gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters for the first time. In defeating the man who ended his US Open title defence earlier this season, the 23-year-old claimed the ninth 1000-level title of his career on Sunday. Unlike their five-set quarterfinal epic in New York two months ago, the clash in Paris lasted just under two hours. “Coming here every year, not finding my best tennis but we never gave up,” Alcaraz said after being handed the trophy for the first time by former Paris Masters winner Boris Becker. “We had really painful losses here and we always said try again,” the Spaniard added with a smile. rejected.title: Eisenkot open to Netanyahu joining Israel’s next government
rejected.description: Israel's president officially tasks the opposition leader with forming a new government.
rejected.excerpt: Israel’s president officially tasks the opposition leader with forming a new government. Israel’s opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, the man officially tasked by President Isaac Herzog with trying to form the country’s next government, has said that he was open to including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his coalition lineup. In a speech at Sunday’s ceremony in Herzog’s office in Jerusalem, Eisenkot suggested Netanyahu’s far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich was also welcome to join. “If members of Likud and the Religious Zionist Party truly believe this is a time for unity, as they told the president, I cannot conceive of any reason why they would not support a government under my leadership and the principles I have presented,” Eisenkot said. Eisenkot, who ran as Netanyahu’s main rival, has six weeks to form a new government. rejected.title: Alcaraz takes revenge on Shelton to win first Paris Masters title
rejected.description: Carlos Alcaraz takes revenge on Ben Shelton as the Spaniard's remarkable comeback from injury continues with victory in the final of the Paris Masters.
rejected.excerpt: Just 60 days after his comeback tournament was ended in a late-night New York blockbuster against Ben Shelton, Carlos Alcaraz took his revenge. In doing so, the Spaniard offered the latest indication that his ascension back to the top of the men's game is nearing completion. Alcaraz exceeded expectations when, on his return from four months out with a wrist injury, he reached the US Open quarter-finals in September before going out in an astonishing five-set epic against rising American star Shelton. In the two months since, Alcaraz has won three titles and lost once in 17 matches. Victory over world number four Shelton on Sunday sealed the 23-year-old's first triumph at the prestigious Paris Masters 1000 tournament. It also confirmed a fully-fit Alcaraz, who has now won seven of the nine ATP Masters 1000 events, will once again be ready to compete for the sport's major prizes in 2027.
